skill.description: Create AI avatar, talking head, and lipsync videos with the inference.sh belt CLI, including portrait-to-video and dubbing workflows.

security_audit.summary: The static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced examples, and the URL findings are documentation or placeholder links. No evidence of command injection, credential theft, or prompt injection was found, but the skill has real privacy and synthetic-media abuse risks.

remediation.issue: Synthetic avatar workflows can enable impersonation or deceptive media.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear consent, authorization, public-figure, and disclosure requirements before generating talking head or lipsync videos.

remediation.issue: Media URLs, scripts, and audio references are sent to hosted inference services.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before sending private assets, and require explicit approval for confidential content or customer data.

remediation.issue: Related skill installation examples may expand the user environment.
remediation.suggestion: State that related npx installation commands must only run after explicit user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Example URLs and Markdown fences trigger noisy automated findings.
remediation.suggestion: Label all placeholder URLs clearly and keep command examples separate from executable automation guidance.

content.user_title: Create AI Avatar Videos with Inference.sh
content.value_statement: Producing presenter videos and localized talking heads can require separate video, voice, and lipsync tools. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through hosted avatar video workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to run P-Video-Avatar with portrait images and text scripts.
Documents optional style, voice, language, and resolution inputs.
Compares P-Video-Avatar, OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse Lipsync use cases.
Outlines workflows for portrait generation, text-to-speech, lipsync, and video dubbing.
Links to inference.sh documentation for running apps and streaming results.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Sends media URLs, text scripts, and audio references to external inference services.
Quality depends on portrait lighting, audio clarity, and model limits.
Does not provide built-in consent, watermarking, or rights verification.

use_cases.title: Product Presenter Videos
use_cases.description: Turn an approved portrait and short script into a presenter-style product walkthrough.

use_cases.title: Training and Explainer Clips
use_cases.description: Create consistent talking head lessons from prepared scripts and authorized speaker assets.

use_cases.title: Localized Dubbing Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan transcription, translation, speech generation, and lipsync steps for multilingual video updates.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Avatar Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one portrait and one script.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ai-avatar-video skill to create a short presenter video from my approved portrait URL and this script: [script]. Use P-Video-Avatar with simple settings.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Right Avatar Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the avatar video models in this skill for my project. I need [duration], [style], [language], and [quality goal]. Recommend one model and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Dubbing Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a step-by-step dubbing plan for this authorized video URL: [video URL]. Include transcription, translation, speech generation, lipsync, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Governed Production Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with safety and approval controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a governed avatar video pipeline for my team. Include consent checks, remote processing approvals, model selection, asset handling, quality review, and disclosure requirements.

output_examples.input: Create a 20-second product demo using an approved portrait and a short launch script.
output_examples.output: Recommended P-Video-Avatar with a 720p portrait, concise script, and English voice. The response requested asset approval before running remote processing.

output_examples.input: Plan a Spanish dubbing workflow for an existing training video.
output: Transcribe the source audio, translate the approved script, generate Spanish speech, run lipsync on the source video, and review timing.
The plan included consent checks and a warning that media is processed by hosted inference apps.

output_examples.input: Compare models for a realistic spokesperson clip with built-in text-to-speech.
output_examples.output: Recommended P-Video-Avatar for speed, cost, built-in voice options, style prompts, and 1080p support. Other models were reserved for special lipsync needs.

best_practices: Use only portraits, voices, and scripts that the requester owns or has permission to use.
Warn users before sending private media or generated transcripts to remote services.
Start with short clips and validate lipsync quality before producing long videos.
anti_patterns: Creating avatars of real people without consent or clear disclosure.
Uploading confidential customer videos or unreleased scripts without approval.
Running related skill installation commands without explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill require inference.sh?
faq.answer: Yes. It is written for the inference.sh belt CLI and requires an authenticated account.

faq.question: Can it generate voice from text?
faq.answer: Yes, P-Video-Avatar includes text-to-speech. Other models may require a separate speech generation step.

faq.question: Does it run video generation locally?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflows call hosted inference apps through the belt CLI.

faq.question: Can it support multilingual dubbing?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill outlines transcription, translation, speech generation, and lipsync steps for dubbing workflows.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What safety checks are important?
faq.answer: Confirm consent, asset rights, disclosure needs, and remote processing approval before creating any synthetic person video.
